construct: the coincident inset ring of pseudo-inset-ring-two-axis, but `[data-appearance="ghost"]::after { display: none }` REMOVES the ring box in a THIRD of the domain — and in exactly those combos the host's own `border-color` is `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`, so a folded width there paints nothing
why: FLUENT BADGE'S MEASURED SHAPE, and the line between the two halves of this class. Replaying the committed capture (extract/computed/out/fluent/badge/captured-truth.json, all 191 `__default` combos): `root::after` is `display: none` in the 48 `ghost` combos and drawn in the other 143, and in every one of those 48 the HOST's own border-{side}-color is rgba(0, 0, 0, 0). Refusing the ring fold on absence ALONE therefore leaves fluent.badge's outline and tint appearances byte-identical to filled forever — the exact census defect this class is named for — while protecting nothing, because a 1px width folded onto a host that paints NO colour in those combos paints no ring. The harm the presence guard exists to prevent needs BOTH halves: no ring box, AND a host colour that inks. pseudo-inset-ring-partial-presence is the companion case where the host DOES ink in the ring-less combos and the fold must still refuse — the two cases pin the two sides of one line. The ring colour is a {appearance}x{tone} PRODUCT over the drawn combos, so the decor grammar's uniform-or-ONE-axis paint factoring refuses and the fold is the only door left.
expectWhere: anatomy.root.literals.border-top-width (folded onto the host beside the border-{side}-color it already carries), with the ring-less combos disclosed by count in the fold receipt

canvas.note: the folded 1px must reach the canvas as a real strokeWeight: without it the host's carried border-{side}-color has no width source and outline/tint draw exactly like ghost. A receipt is not a ring, so this case declares mustDraw.
